headline: 5 Questions Careful Buyers Should Ask Before Buying A Home Cabin
dek: A plain look at the price and what holds up once the box arrives, without a sales call.
lede: What should you check before a cabin like this comes home? The answers start below.

reasons.heading: What a careful buyer checks first, part 1
reasons.text: rarely come from a single glossy photo or a catchy headline; they come from spending a few careful minutes comparing specifics side by side across the handful of options actually worth considering (bravo). A shopper who has been burned before learns to slow down and read past the marketing copy, looking instead for plain language about materials, construction, and the kind of support a company offers once the sale is already done and the box has arrived at the front door (bravo). What separates a brand worth trusting from one that just talks a good game usually shows up in the small details (bravo): how it answers a direct question, whether its claims line up with what it actually publishes, and how it treats a customer who asks something inconvenient before buying (bravo). for_you.text: You have a dry, level corner of a room you can give up for good.
You would rather read the published specification than book a sales call.
You want a session you can take without leaving the house.

not_for_you.text: You rent and cannot leave a cabin behind when the lease ends.
Your only free wall is in an unheated garage that freezes in winter.
You want something that folds away between sessions.
